legs.leg: diagnostic probe: forceUpdateCollection ordering and locking
legs.result: testForceUpdateCollectionSyncsBeforeReads: against a live single ZkTestServer, a collection state written directly to ZooKeeper while the update lock kept it unpublished locally; after clearing the spy's recorded invocations, forceUpdateCollection refreshed it, and Mockito InOrder verified zkClient.sync(COLLECTIONS_ZKNODE) was invoked before the getData read of that collection's state path. testForceUpdateCollectionDoesNotHoldUpdateLockWhileSyncWaits: with the sync callback withheld, another thread acquired reader.getUpdateLock() within 5 s while forceUpdateCollection was still waiting in sync; firing the callback with CONNECTIONLOSS then surfaced KeeperException.ConnectionLossException out of forceUpdateCollection before any read. The probe's first two attempts failed on probe-harness defects only (missing JUnit import wiring, then an ObjectTracker release through the Mockito spy instead of the constructed client instance); both are visible in the run history and the final source in evidence is the version that passed. The probe is a diagnostic against a single-server ensemble, as the gate specifies; it does not prove ensemble lag behavior, and the branch's own testSync remains a single-server smoke test.

summary: The tidy successor head passes the full split-sync gate. The named suites match the gated head's counts (SolrZkClientTest 8/8 including testSync, ZkStateReaderTest 16/16, TestInPlaceUpdatesDistrib 1/1, no skips), root tidy now leaves zero tracked changes, and root check -x test passes (the UI wasm zip was seeded by curl after verifying its SHA-256 against the gradle.properties pin, the established remedy for the egress relay corrupting that download). The disposable diagnostic probe, adapted from the prior combined-branch ClusterStateProviderTest.testSyncWaitsForCallbackAndPropagatesFailure at 5da7243, demonstrates all four required behaviors against this head: SolrZkClient.sync waits for its callback and maps a callback error to the matching KeeperException; sync honors interruption promptly; forceUpdateCollection invokes sync before its collection-state read (Mockito InOrder against a live single ZooKeeper); and forceUpdateCollection does not hold getUpdateLock while the sync waits (the lock was acquired from another thread mid-wait, and the sync error then surfaced from forceUpdateCollection before any read). This is a single-server diagnostic; no ensemble-lag claim is made.
